findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file-not-found, permission-denied, or encoding error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric or malformed numeric value
findings.failure_mode: a single bad field in the CSV aborts the entire parse, losing all previously parsed records
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(...)) and propagate through the Result typechain

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy downcast from u32; values >65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a legitimate metric value of 70000 silently becomes 4434, corrupting downstream calculations with no signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange) or parse directly as u16 via str::parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside the parsing/calculation core
findings.failure_mode: the data-loading function has a side effect (stdout write) that cannot be suppressed in production, violates functional-core imperative-shell boundary, and produces nondeterministic output
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the core; if metrics/telemetry are needed, pass a callback or reporter trait into the shell layer outside the pure parse path

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] index into a Vec without bounds check; a line with fewer than 2 commas panics
findings.failure_mode: any short or malformed CSV line (empty line, trailing newline, single-field line) causes a runtime panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: check parts.len() >= 2 before indexing, or use get(0).ok_or(...) and get(1).ok_or(...) to return a typed MissingField error

findings.problem: line.split(',').collect() into Vec<String> allocates unnecessarily and violates the mandatory split_once pattern for one-separator grammars
findings.failure_mode: every line allocates a Vec of Strings and a trimmed String for each part, wasting memory and CPU; no max-items cap means unbounded allocation from adversarial input
findings.fix: use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MalformedLine)?; then parse value_str.trim() directly; enforce a max-items cap with try_reserve before collection

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String (raw primitive) and pub value: u16 (raw primitive) with no domain validation
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with an empty name, negative-looking value, or otherwise invalid state because there are no invariants enforced at the type level; illegal states are representable
findings.fix: use a Name newtype with a smart constructor that rejects empty strings; enforce value range at construction; make fields private behind a constructor that returns Result or Self validated by type invariants

findings.problem: raw primitive &str crosses the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; load_metrics accepts hostile input and constructs domain values unsafely
findings.failure_mode: callers can pass arbitrary paths and the function produces domain values through a chain of panics and lossy casts, so no caller can rely on Record being a valid domain type
findings.fix: define a Result-returning parse_boundary function that reads the file safely, splits with split_once, validates each field, and constructs trusted domain types; load_metrics delegates to this boundary

findings.problem: load_metrics has no max-items cap, no try_reserve, and no input size limit
findings.failure_mode: an adversarial or misconfigured file can trigger unbounded heap allocation, leading to OOM denial-of-service
findings.fix: accept a max_items: usize parameter; validate file size or line count against it; call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| AllocationError::Exceeded)? after cap validation

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, and domain construction into a single function, violating Data/Calculations/Actions architecture
findings.failure_mode: the pure parsing/calculation logic cannot be tested in isolation, reused without file access, or composed with alternative data sources; the function mixes shell concerns (file reading) with core concerns (parsing, validation)
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>; (2) a shell fn load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads the file, calls parse_line per line, and handles allocation

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failure modes are collapsed into panic surfaces
findings.failure_mode: the caller cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from overflow from OOM, preventing targeted recovery or retry logic
findings.fix: define an enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), MalformedLine(usize), InvalidValue { field: usize, cause: ParseIntError }, ValueOutOfRange(usize) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>
